message: No detected untrusted source handling: The code downloads data via wget from a hardcoded URL (CONFIG['url']) with no checksum verification, signature check, or authentication of the source.
No detected label flipping detection: The code loads and uses labels without any checks for label distribution, validation against expected label sets, or label-noise detection tools.

No detected data poisoning defenses: The data preparation only applies StandardScaler normalization and forward/backward fill for NaN values, with no outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or filtering of suspicious inputs.

No detected model integrity verification: The code checks for an existing .pth file path but never performs any hash check, signature verification, or pinned revision when loading serialized model weights.
No detected label distribution validation: No code checks class balance, expected label sets, or anomalous sample distributions before or during training.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no trigger detection, activation analysis, or gradient anomaly detection anywhere in the training pipeline.
No detected differential privacy: No differential privacy library (Opacus, TF Privacy, DP-SGD) or mechanism is used in the training code.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: There is no use of adversarial attack libraries (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD) or any adversarial input generation in the evaluation code.

No detected metric tampering protection: Although separate validation datasets are used (ADL4/ADL5 vs. training splits), there is no signed/hashed evaluation data, no cryptographic isolation, and no multiple independent metric sources to guard against metric manipulation.
No detected input sanitization: The inference path (validate function and data loaders) applies no shape, range, or schema validation on incoming data before passing it to the model.
No detected output bounds checks: The code computes accuracy and loss from model outputs but performs no NaN guards, probability sanity checks, or bounds validation on the scores before using them.
No detected prompt injection defenses: This is a time-series sensor data model (CPC), not an LLM, so prompt-injection defenses are not applicable and none are implemented.
